name: Accessibility / convenience
definition: Reducing practical, geographic, scheduling, or delivery barriers so that a target behavior is easier to perform.

syntheses.design: network meta-analysis of randomized recipient-focused vaccine uptake interventions
syntheses.notes: Access interventions improved vaccine uptake. Accessibility is kept separate from affordability because the source network meta-analysis estimates them independently.

name: Affordability
definition: Reducing the direct financial cost of performing or obtaining the target behavior or service.

syntheses.design: network meta-analysis of randomized recipient-focused vaccine uptake interventions
syntheses.notes: Affordability interventions improved vaccine uptake. This is not the same as paying a contingent reward; it reduces the cost of action.

name: Anticipated regret
definition: Expected regret about performing or failing to perform a behavior before the behavioral choice occurs.

syntheses.design: random-effects meta-analysis of 81 studies
syntheses.notes: Association with behavior; anticipated regret was also associated with intention at r=0.50. Not causal evidence.

name: Autonomous motivation
definition: Motivation experienced as volitional and self-endorsed rather than controlled by pressure.

syntheses.design: change meta-analysis of randomized interventions that successfully increased autonomous motivation
syntheses.notes: Behavior effect among tests with significant target engagement; target change itself was d=0.64.

name: Behavioral attitudes
definition: Evaluation of performing a specific behavior as favorable or unfavorable.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental tests that successfully changed the target construct
syntheses.notes: Only behavior-specific evaluations belong here; broad object attitudes remain separate.

name: Default options
definition: Choice architectures in which one option is pre-selected and is implemented unless the decision-maker actively chooses another option.

syntheses.behavior_domain: consumer, environmental, health and other decisions
syntheses.design: meta-analysis of 58 default studies
syntheses.notes: Substantial heterogeneity; three-level model estimate was d+=0.63 [0.47,0.80].

name: Education / information provision
definition: Providing factual or explanatory information intended to improve understanding relevant to a target behavior.

syntheses.design: network meta-analysis of randomized recipient-focused vaccine uptake interventions
syntheses.notes: Education interventions improved vaccine uptake in this domain. This is an intervention strategy, not proof that measured knowledge itself is the causal mediator.

name: Fear appeals
definition: Persuasive communications that deliberately depict or evoke fear or threat to influence attitudes, intentions, or behavior.

syntheses.design: random-effects meta-analysis of experimental fear-appeal studies
syntheses.notes: Primary reported effect is a composite across attitudes, intentions, and behaviors, so it must not be ranked as a behavior-only effect without extracting the behavior subgroup.

name: Financial incentives
definition: Material monetary rewards contingent on performing a target behavior or achieving a target outcome.

syntheses.design: systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled incentive interventions
syntheses.notes: All behaviors combined; effectiveness tended to attenuate with longer post-intervention follow-up.

syntheses.outcome: habitual health behavior change at up to 18 months
syntheses.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of adult randomized trials
syntheses.notes: Effect at up to 18 months from baseline; effects generally weakened after incentive removal.

name: Goal setting
definition: Specifying a desired behavioral or outcome standard to guide action.

syntheses.design: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials isolating the unique effect of goal setting
syntheses.notes: 384 effect sizes from 141 papers; k here denotes extracted effect sizes.

name: Habit / behavioral automaticity
definition: A learned cue-response tendency in which behavior becomes increasingly automatic through repetition in recurring contexts.

syntheses.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of Self-Report Habit Index applications
syntheses.notes: Medium-to-strong association; much of the evidence is observational, so this should not be ranked as causal evidence.

name: Identity / self-identity
definition: The extent to which a behavior, role, or goal is represented as part of the self-concept. This folder keeps identity constructs distinct from habit and intention while documenting overlaps.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis
syntheses.notes: Self-identity association with behavioral intention; this is not a direct identity-behavior causal estimate.

syntheses.design: systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
syntheses.notes: Identity-habit association, not identity-behavior. Preserved because it is frequently misinterpreted.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental and quasi-experimental interventions
syntheses.notes: Effect on identity itself. Behavior changed in the same intervention literature, but this estimate alone does not establish identity as the mediator.

name: Implementation intentions
definition: Plans that link a specified situational cue to a goal-directed response in an if-then form.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of 94 independent experimental tests
syntheses.notes: Medium-to-large effect; review also reports enhanced cue accessibility and more automatic goal-directed responding.

name: Behavioral intentions
definition: A stated commitment or readiness to perform a specified behavior.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of 47 experimental tests in which randomized interventions significantly changed intention
syntheses.notes: A medium-to-large intention change (d=0.66) was followed by a small-to-medium behavior change (d=0.36).

name: Perceived competence
definition: Perceived effectiveness or competence in carrying out a target behavior, especially in Self-Determination Theory contexts.

syntheses.design: change meta-analysis of randomized interventions that successfully increased perceived competence
syntheses.notes: Related to self-efficacy but retained as a separate construct; target change itself was d=0.36.

name: Prompts and reminders
definition: External visual, verbal, digital, or contextual cues that draw attention to a target behavior at a relevant moment.

syntheses.design: pre-registered multilevel meta-analysis of prompt interventions
syntheses.notes: Model coefficient summarizes Hedges-g effect sizes across 61 studies; unconfounded prompt interventions yielded a nearly identical estimate (b=0.66).

syntheses.design: network meta-analysis of randomized recipient-focused vaccine uptake interventions
syntheses.notes: Reminder interventions increased vaccination uptake; moderate-certainty network meta-analysis evidence.

name: Punishment
definition: Imposed negative consequences contingent on noncooperation or undesired behavior.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental social-dilemma studies
syntheses.notes: Medium-to-large positive effect on cooperation. This is not equivalent to legal/administrative sanctions in real-world compliance settings.

name: Risk appraisal
definition: A prospective appraisal of threat or harm, including perceived risk, severity, anticipatory emotion, and anticipated emotion.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experiments that significantly increased risk appraisal before measuring behavior
syntheses.notes: Direct target-change evidence. Intention effect was d=0.31 (k=217). Combined increases in risk appraisal, response efficacy, and self-efficacy yielded a larger behavior effect (d=0.45).

name: Self-efficacy
definition: Belief in one's capability to organize and execute the actions required to perform a target behavior.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental tests that successfully changed the target construct
syntheses.notes: Kept separate from perceived competence despite conceptual overlap.

name: Self-monitoring of behavior
definition: Systematically observing or recording one's own target behavior in order to make behavior salient and support regulation.

syntheses.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 19 randomized intervention studies using self-monitoring
syntheses.notes: Interventions using self-monitoring reduced total sedentary time; attribution to self-monitoring alone is limited because some interventions were multicomponent.

name: Social norms
definition: Perceived or communicated standards about what others do or approve.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental tests that successfully changed the target construct
syntheses.notes: Norm subtypes stay explicit and may later split when separate pooled estimates are available.

name: Social support
definition: Interpersonal resources that provide informational, emotional, affirmational, or tangible assistance relevant to performing a target behavior.

syntheses.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
syntheses.notes: Moderate heterogeneity (I2=58.3%). Estimate is domain-specific and should not be generalized to all behaviors without additional syntheses.

name: Trust in healthcare professionals
definition: A patient's trust in a healthcare professional or clinician within a treatment relationship.

syntheses.design: random-effects meta-analysis of observational studies
syntheses.notes: Small association with health behaviors. Authors explicitly note that prospective work is needed; not causal evidence.
